description: Build the homepage narrative top half: redesign steps 3-11 (hero, product hero composition, trust/integration strip, platform story, team use cases tabbed, Companions, Rooms, Routines, Artifacts). Replace the current Landing.jsx with a new editorial homepage that reuses AmazAI's real product UI as the primary visual language via lightweight static compositions built from the Companion system and product-frame markup. Depends on FEAT-001 (tokens + nav). All sections must make AmazAI understandable BEFORE introducing its terminology.
steps: Replace web/src/screens/Landing.jsx so it renders (in order) TopNav, the new hero, then each homepage section below, then PublicFooter. Keep the <Seo> tag (update title/description to reflect the new positioning) and keep the route wiring in main.jsx unchanged (/welcome-to-amazai under <PublicOnly>). Prefer composing sections as small components in a new folder web/src/screens/home/ (e.g. Hero.jsx, ProductFrame.jsx, TrustStrip.jsx, PlatformStory.jsx, TeamUseCases.jsx, Companions.jsx, Rooms.jsx, Routines.jsx, Artifacts.jsx) imported by Landing.jsx, so the file stays readable and later features can add more sections. Give each major section a stable id anchor (companions, rooms, routines, artifacts, connectors, etc.) so the nav mega-menu links resolve.

STEP 3 (hero): Large editorial hero. Headline exactly: `Your work has a new operating system.` Supporting copy exactly: `Build a team of AI companions that can research, create, use your tools, run recurring work, and collaborate with you from one workspace.` Primary CTA `Start for free` (startLogin signup:true returnTo:'/welcome'). Secondary CTA `See how it works` (link to /how-it-works or homepage #platform anchor). Microcopy exactly: `No credit card required · Set up in minutes`. Use responsive clamp() type. Do NOT use an abstract AI illustration as the primary visual.

STEP 4 (product hero composition): Build the hero artwork as a lightweight STATIC recreation of the AmazAI workspace (do NOT import the live app Shell/Room which need api/auth). Compose a product frame showing: application sidebar, workspace, rooms, companions (use the Companion component with real archetypes/states), a prompt/composer, live companion activity, and artifact creation. Reference the real surfaces (Room.jsx, Rooms.jsx, Sidebar.jsx, Composer.jsx, Sections.jsx, PresenceFeed/CoordinationFeed) for layout vocabulary and class-style, but render it as self-contained marketing markup + CSS. The product should feel alive (selective CSS motion, e.g. a companion in `working`/`thinking` state, an activity line appearing) without scroll-jacking or parallax and respecting prefers-reduced-motion.

STEP 5 (trust/integration strip): Immediately after the hero. Headline exactly: `One workspace. Your models, tools, files, teammates, and AI companions.` Show supported tool logos: GitHub, Google Drive, Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, Notion, Microsoft. Only show integrations that actually exist or are clearly marked 'upcoming' - check docs/connectors.md and screens/marketing/Integrations.jsx for which are real; mark any not-yet-real ones with an explicit 'Upcoming' tag. Use simple inline SVG or text wordmarks (do NOT fabricate partnership claims). Keep restrained (no giant pills).

STEP 6 (platform story): A storytelling transition section. Eyebrow exactly: `AI shouldn't just answer questions.` Headline exactly: `It should get the work done.` Build an interactive/animated workflow (CSS + small React state or IntersectionObserver; NO heavy libs) explaining coordination for the example request `Prepare our Monday growth meeting.`: show delegation to Marketing Companion (Pulls campaign performance), Research Companion (Finds competitor changes), Operations Companion (Reviews relevant business metrics); then outputs Weekly Growth Brief, Competitive Update, Meeting Agenda; then `Routine scheduled for next Monday`. Use the Companion avatars and product-frame styling. The user must grasp multi-agent coordination without technical architecture terms.

STEP 7 (team use cases): Tabbed section. Headline exactly: `Built for the work happening across your company.` Tabs: Founders, Marketing, Sales, Operations, Product, Engineering. Selecting a tab changes copy, example prompt, workflow, and the adjacent product preview. Use the exact per-team descriptions from the user spec (FOUNDERS: Research markets, prepare meetings, track priorities, and keep projects moving. MARKETING: Research competitors, create campaigns, repurpose content, and monitor performance. SALES: Research accounts, prepare calls, draft follow-ups, and maintain pipeline context. OPERATIONS: Automate recurring workflows and move information between systems. PRODUCT: Synthesize feedback, create specs, research competitors, and monitor releases. ENGINEERING: Investigate issues, research repositories, create implementation plans, and coordinate technical work.). Tabs must remain usable on mobile (scrollable/segmented, no overflow) with proper ARIA tab roles + keyboard support.

STEP 8 (Companions): Large alternating product section. Headline exactly: `Build the team you need.` Explain companions have roles, instructions, tools, context, and ongoing responsibility. Show a companion profile and a companion actively working (reuse Companion states + AgentProfile-style static frame). id=companions.

STEP 9 (Rooms): Alternating section. Headline exactly: `Give work a place to live.` Show a room containing people, companions, messages, files, routines, and artifacts (static recreation informed by Room.jsx/RoomInfo.jsx). id=rooms.

STEP 10 (Routines): Alternating section. Headline exactly: `Turn repeated work into something that runs itself.` Show a real routine configuration and execution timeline. Example: `Competitive Intelligence` / `Every Monday · 8:00 AM` with steps Research competitors, Analyze meaningful changes, Update brief, Notify Marketing (informed by Sections.jsx Routines + Timeline.jsx). id=routines.

STEP 11 (Artifacts): MAJOR dedicated section - one of the strongest moments on the site. Headline exactly: `Finished work, not disappearing chat responses.` Explain companions create durable outputs: documents, research, spreadsheets, plans, reports, images, code, and other files. Show a beautiful artifact library and artifact viewer (static recreation informed by Sections.jsx Artifacts). id=artifacts.

Add all supporting CSS to styles.css (or a dedicated import) under the marketing token layer. Use alternating large sections (not endless bento grids, not purple-on-purple, no glassmorphism-everywhere, no glowing orbs). Purple used selectively.
Keep the homepage understandable to a first-time visitor before AmazAI terminology is introduced. Re-run build and tests after implementing; keep green.
acceptance_criteria: Visiting /welcome-to-amazai renders the new editorial homepage with the hero headline 'Your work has a new operating system.' and all exact copy strings from the spec (hero supporting copy, CTAs, microcopy, section headlines, eyebrows).
The hero product composition uses real Companion components and product-frame markup (not a generic AI illustration) and shows sidebar/workspace/rooms/companions/composer/activity/artifact.
The trust strip shows only real-or-marked-upcoming integrations with the exact headline.
The team use cases section is tabbed with all six teams and the exact descriptions, and tabs are keyboard/ARIA accessible.
Sections Companions/Rooms/Routines/Artifacts exist with exact headlines and stable id anchors matching the nav mega-menu.
Motion (if any) is CSS-based, selective, respects prefers-reduced-motion, and no new heavy animation dependency was added to package.json.
npm run build is clean and npm test passes after the changes.
verification: cd /projects/sandbox/AmazAI/web && export NVM_DIR=/root/.nvm && . /root/.nvm/nvm.sh && npm run build
git diff --stat to confirm package.json has no new runtime dependency.
findings:
Replaced Landing.jsx with a new editorial homepage (root carries `.mkt`, keeps <Seo> + TopNav + PublicFooter). Sections built as small components in NEW web/src/screens/home/: Hero.jsx, ProductFrame.jsx, TrustStrip.jsx, PlatformStory.jsx, TeamUseCases.jsx, Companions.jsx, Rooms.jsx, Routines.jsx, Artifacts.jsx, plus useReveal.js (a single-boolean IntersectionObserver hook). All CSS appended to web/src/styles.css under the existing `.mkt` marketing layer (reuses FEAT-001 tokens/primitives; no new files/deps).

STEPS 3-11 delivered with verbatim copy:
- (3) Hero: 'Your work has a new operating system.' + exact supporting copy; Start for free -> startLogin(signup:true,returnTo:'/welcome'); See how it works -> Link /how-it-works; microcopy 'No credit card required · Set up in minutes'. clamp() type.
- (4) ProductFrame: static recreation of the workspace (sidebar+workspace badge, rooms list, companions via real Companion component, room header w/ avatars, live activity lines that slide in, artifact assembling w/ progress bar, composer). No live-app imports; role=img w/ descriptive aria-label.
- (5) TrustStrip: exact headline. HONESTY: only Slack is real per docs/connectors.md + Integrations.jsx; GitHub/Google Drive/Gmail/Google Calendar/Notion/Microsoft each carry an explicit 'Upcoming' tag. Plain text wordmarks, no fabricated logos/partnerships.
- (6) PlatformStory: eyebrow 'AI shouldn’t just answer questions.' + headline 'It should get the work done.'; 'Prepare our Monday growth meeting.' fans out to the three named companions/tasks, three outputs (Weekly Growth Brief/Competitive Update/Meeting Agenda), then 'Routine scheduled for next Monday'. Staggered CSS entrance keyed off useReveal.
- (7) TeamUseCases: exact headline + all six teams' exact descriptions. Real ARIA tablist/tab/tabpanel with roving tabIndex + Arrow/Home/End keyboard (automatic activation); strip is horizontally scrollable on mobile (no overflow). Swaps copy, example prompt, mini-workflow, and adjacent product preview.
- (8) Companions id=companions: 'Build the team you need.' + profile frame (role/tools/context/responsibility) beside a working state.
- (9) Rooms id=rooms (alternating, art-left): 'Give work a place to live.' room frame w/ people+companions, messages, files, routines, artifacts.
- (10) Routines id=routines: 'Turn repeated work into something that runs itself.' Competitive Intelligence / Every Monday · 8:00 AM config + timeline (Research competitors, Analyze meaningful changes, Update brief, Notify Marketing).
- (11) Artifacts id=artifacts (the big moment): 'Finished work, not disappearing chat responses.' names documents/research/spreadsheets/plans/reports/images/code/other files; artifact library grid + artifact viewer (doc + bar chart).

MOTION: CSS transitions/keyframes + one IntersectionObserver boolean only; no new deps (git diff --stat web/package.json = empty). prefers-reduced-motion block stills all entrances to their final legible state. DESIGN restraint: white canvas, alternating sections, two washed bands (story + artifacts) so it is not purple-on-purple, no orbs/glass/bento.

TESTS: added web/src/screens/Landing.test.jsx (mocks ../auth0 like Pricing.test.jsx; asserts hero copy + Start for free CTA, the four anchor ids, and tablist keyboard nav). Suite: 29 files / 197 tests passing (was 194). npm run build clean. Pricing.test.jsx untouched and green.

DEVIATIONS/NOTES: 'See how it works' points to the existing /how-it-works route (spec allowed that or the #platform anchor; PlatformStory still carries id=platform for the nav). Team-tab preview tints use color-mix with a solid gradient fallback line first. Steps 12-18 (FEAT-003) and mobile/a11y/SEO/perf deep polish (FEAT-004) intentionally not done. Old .landing-* CSS left in place (now unused by the homepage; harmless, avoids touching unrelated selectors).
